analyst_view.overall: Granada are 4th (27 points from 14) and unbeaten in seven under Pacheta, though an eight-game winning run across all competitions ended with a 1-1 at Sabadell. Ceuta are bottom with 5 points, 35 goals conceded and five straight defeats, the latest 2-3 at home to leaders Almería in which Cedric Teguia scored and was then sent off; his ban is confirmed by EFE and counted by the numbers, as is Jordi Escobar's season-ending knee injury. Ceuta's new coach Sergio Lobera (since 12 November) wants possession and attacking football, and their recent games under him, with many shots and corners, are in the numbers. Owen is away on Spain youth duty rather than injured; the earlier report that Granada's Alejandro Marqués trained apart could not be confirmed this time, so I no longer adjust for it. No referee is named, and news for this match was thin (no preview or press conference could be read).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 2.0 for Granada, already adding for Ceuta's leaky run (15 conceded in six) and taking about 22% off Ceuta for Escobar and 5% for Teguia's ban. My earlier small cut for Marqués' fitness rested on one report I could not confirm this time, so I drop it and stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and already move a lot for recent form: down for Granada's very low count (13 in six) and up 13% for Ceuta's high one under Lobera (51 in six). Rival coaches call Granada strong at set pieces, but that is their usual game and in their record, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.7 cards and already add 11% for Ceuta's recent bookings, including Teguia's red against Almería; Ceuta have 41 yellows and 3 reds, Granada 30 and none. No referee is named and nothing else points either way, so I stay at 5.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots and already lift Ceuta's attempts a lot (111 in six, +24%), which fits Lobera's attacking style, though some of that volume came while chasing games. Granada have shot less than usual lately (62 in six), also counted, so I stay at about 26.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target and already credit both sides' recent accuracy (+6% Granada, +11% Ceuta). With no confirmed absences in Granada's attack and Ceuta's missing forwards counted, I stay at 9.4.
